This Appeal, Coming On For Orders, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is by the claimant being the wife of the first respondent, who is the owner of the offending vehicle namely, motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53/V-63631 which was ridden by the son of the claimant and respondent No.1.
2.

The claimant stated to have been traveling as a pillion rider on the said motorcycle on 28.06.2015 with her son being the rider of the said motorcycle, who due to his negligence applied sudden brake resulting in claimant falling from the motorcycle on to the road sustaining fracture of shaft of tibia and fibula and other grievous injuries to the different parts of the body.

Upon the claim being made by the claimant for a compensation of NC: 2023:KHC-K:8562 Rs.16,00,000/- on the ground of she earning Rs.12,000/- per month being agricultural labour and house wife, the Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.1,95,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit and directed respondent No.1-owner of the vehicle to pay the compensation on the premise that the rider of the motorcycle namely, Irfan, the son of the claimant and respondent No.1 did not pocess valid and effective driving licnece to ride the motorcycle.

Being aggrieved by the same, the claimant is before this Court, wherein apart from seeking enhancement of compensation, she is seeking for an order directing respondent No.2 - Insurance Company to pay the compensation.

3. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of PAPPU AND OTHERS VS. VINOD KUMAR LAMBA AND ANOTHER reported in (2018) 3 SCC 208 at paragraphs 12 and 17 has held as under:
NC: 2023:KHC-K:8562 "12.

entities.text: PAPPU AND OTHERS VS. VINOD KUMAR LAMBA AND ANOTHER reported in (2018) 3 SCC 208
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd.
(supra), has noticed the defences available to the Insurance Company under Section 149(2)(a)(ii) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
The Insurance Company is entitled to take a defence that the offending vehicle was driven by an unauthorised person or the person driving the vehicle did not have a valid driving licence.

The onus would shift on the Insurance Company only after the owner of the offending vehicle pleads and Smt. Gousabee vs Sri. Mohammed Patel And Anr on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177096100/
2 proves the basic facts within his knowledge that the driver of the offending vehicle was authorised by him to drive the vehicle and was having a valid driving licence at the relevant time.

entities.text: Smt. Gousabee vs Sri. Mohammed Patel And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
17. This issue has been answered in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd.
(supra).

In that case, it was contended by the insurance company that once the defence taken by the insurer is accepted by the Tribunal, it is bound to discharge the insurer and fix the liability only on the owner and/or the driver of the vehicle.

However, this Court held that even if the insurer succeeds in establishing its defence,
the Tribunal or the Court can direct the insurance company to pay the award amount to the claimant(s) and, in turn, recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

NC: 2023:KHC-K:8562 The three-Judge Bench, after analysing the earlier decisions on the point,
held that there was no reason to deviate from the said well-settled principle".
4.

In the instant case, there appears to be no pleading or evidence produced by the claimant or respondent No.1 regarding the rider of the motorcycle possessing valid and prescribed driving licence to ride the motorcycle in question.

In view of the aforesaid law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, the burden of proving the same was on the claimant or the owner of the vehicle namely,
respondent No.1.
That having not been discharged, the finding of the Tribunal fastening the liability on respondent No.1 cannot be found fault with.

5. As regards the plea of pay and recovery is concerned, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Balu Krishna Chavan vs. The Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd. & Ors. reported in 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 932 has held that the order for pay and recovery cannot be passed in a routine manner, the direction has to be NC: 2023:KHC-K:8562 issued only if the facts and circumstances of the case warrants.

entities.text: Balu Krishna Chavan vs. The Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd. & Ors. reported in 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 932
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, claimant being the wife of respondent No.1 and the rider of the motorcycle being the son of claimant and respondent No.1, no material evidence is placed on record to show that the claimant is not having any source to immediately meet her requirement.
In that view of the matter, applying the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court in the case of Balu Krishna Chavan (supra), there is no merit in the appeal warranting interference.
The same is accordingly dismissed.
